nodes.name: Ground locomotion
nodes.purpose: Ground gait choice, analog input shaping, the ramp that walks speed toward its target, gait animation tiering and the 180 degree quick turn

nodes.name: Velocity integration and world response
nodes.purpose: Velocity integration and the world rules applied to it: gravity, damping, horizontal and vertical clamps, and the per-surface modifiers that change friction, sink depth and periodic damage

nodes.name: Air and water modes
nodes.purpose: Airborne and swimming motion: the jump and fall control mode, terminal-fall bookkeeping, buoyancy near the water surface, water current drift and the staff boost lift

nodes.name: Staff combat
nodes.purpose: Staff attack selection and chaining, the guard stance, incoming hit response, knockback bookkeeping and the health pool that ends the run

nodes.name: Magic meter and spells
nodes.purpose: Magic meter and its caps, the availability gates for each staff spell, charge accumulation and the scarab wallet that funds the bag upgrades

nodes.name: Wall, ladder and ledge traversal
nodes.purpose: Wall climb, ladder and ledge traversal: wall probes, climb speed from stick magnitude, ledge grab and the accelerating ladder slide

nodes.name: Camera
nodes.purpose: Camera state, projection setup, per-update shake and far-plane fades, plus the reticle target scan and the mode blend that decides what the player is aiming at

nodes.name: Frame clock and loop order
nodes.purpose: Frame clock and loop order: normalises elapsed milliseconds into a 60 Hz delta, clamps long frames, then updates input, objects, camera, audio and render

cards.name: Ground speed tiers
cards.summary: The moving state writes one speed cap that depends on mode flags: ground, airborne flags, aim overlay and water each have their own cap
cards.behavior: The moving state writes a single speed cap before it moves the character. With none of the special flags set the cap is 2.3993998 speed units per update. When one of two airborne-type flags is set it is 1.9. While a look or aim overlay flag is set the cap is 2.0, or 0.8 in the branch that also has the swim-type flag set. The same swim-type branch without the overlay uses 1.1996999. The flag meanings are inferred from their effects. The wanted speed is the cap minus a 0.05 trim, times the shaped stick magnitude (see the input shaping card) and times a per-move speed scale, so an animation set can bias one move faster or slower without changing the cap. The wanted speed is then approached by the ramp card. A branch that has no root motion uses it as horizontal velocity; whether root motion consumes it elsewhere is not shown in these lines.

constants.name: groundSpeedCap
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: airborneSpeedCap
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: aimSpeedCapOnLand
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: speedCapTrim
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

capabilities: one speed cap per mode flag

cards.name: Stick shaping and move gate
cards.summary: Stick magnitude loses a dead zone, is rescaled onto the cap, and must clear its own gate before walking starts
cards.behavior: The analog magnitude is never used raw in the moving state. A dead zone of 0.2 is subtracted and the remainder is divided by 0.8, then clamped to the range 0 to 1, so the top four fifths of the stick travel carry all of the speed. That value multiplies the speed cap and the per-move speed scale to give the wanted speed. In the idle state, handing over to the moving state needs a tracked magnitude field and the live magnitude both at or above 0.22 and the current animation speed at or above the move table entry threshold, so a small tilt does not start a walk.

constants.name: stickDeadZone
constants.unit: stick magnitude, 0 to 1

constants.name: stickRescaleSpan
constants.unit: stick magnitude, 0 to 1

constants.name: moveStartMagnitudeGate
constants.unit: stick magnitude, 0 to 1

cards.name: Velocity ramp and gait tiers
cards.summary: Wanted speed is approached with a per-update change capped at 0.1 times the frame delta, and a tier counter in steps of 4 follows the speed through a threshold table
cards.behavior: Speed is not assigned directly. Each update the controller takes the gap between the wanted speed and the current animation speed, passes it through an exponential approach with the move smoothing rate, and clamps the change for that update to 0.1 times the frame delta. When the character is turning hard (turn rate at or above 0x96) and the change is positive, it is replaced by minus twice its size so the speed drops during a sharp turn. The current speed is then clamped between a move-table floor and the speed cap. A separate tier counter, stored in steps of 4, rises by 4 when the speed reaches the next entry in the move threshold table and the speed is below the cap, falls by 4 when the speed drops under the current entry, and drops control back to the idle state when it is at the lowest tier with speed and stick both low. Entering the moving state sets the velocity smoothing time to 8.

constants.name: speedChangeCapPerUpdate
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: gaitTierStep
constants.unit: tier counter units

constants.name: moveStartSmoothingTime
constants.unit: smoothing time field set on entering the moving state (units unverified)

cards.name: Quick turn
cards.summary: A hard reversal at speed in a narrow move-progress window plays a spin that flips the heading half a turn and negates the animation speeds
cards.behavior: The quick turn fires only while the move progress is between 0.1 and 0.25, the current animation speed is above a move-table entry minus 0.4, the stick magnitude is above 0.8 and the signed turn rate is at or above 0x96 binary angle units. When these hold, the heading is flipped by half a turn (0x8000), the current and the first animation speed fields are negated so the momentum carries into the spin, the event step spacing is set to 16, and the animation rate is set to 0.2 plus two move-table values and the current speed, divided by 30. The heading is locked while the move runs, and control returns when both animation speed fields have fallen to a move-table exit value.

constants.name: quickTurnInputGate
constants.unit: stick magnitude, 0 to 1

constants.name: quickTurnRateGate
constants.unit: binary angle units, signed turn rate field, rate unverified

constants.name: quickTurnEventSpacing
constants.unit: frames of event step spacing

constants.name: quickTurnRateDivisor
constants.unit: divisor of the animation rate, dimensionless

constants.name: quickTurnHeadingFlip
constants.unit: binary angle units, 65536 per turn

cards.name: Jump and airborne pose
cards.summary: The airborne state writes vertical velocity from a stored launch value, maps it onto one jump animation, and nudges the heading while the stick is held
cards.behavior: The airborne state writes vertical velocity as a stored vertical value times the frame delta. That value is set by outside code through a setter, so scripted jumps and item-driven launches share this flight code, and the state returns control at once when the stored value is zero. This state shows no gravity step, so any arc shaping happens where the value is updated. The jump animation position is one minus the clamp of (1 plus the vertical value) divided by 2, so a rising body sits at the start of the move and a falling body at the end. While the stick magnitude is above 0.1 the target heading is nudged by the stored turn rate times the frame delta, divided by 32 and converted at 182.044 binary angle units per degree. The state also sets a hit probe distance field to 10 and a velocity smoothing time of 16.

constants.name: airborneHitProbeDistance
constants.unit: world units written to a hit probe distance field

constants.name: airborneSmoothingTime
constants.unit: velocity smoothing time field (units unverified)

constants.name: airbornePoseDivisor
constants.unit: divisor applied to one plus the vertical value

constants.name: binaryAnglePerDegree
constants.unit: binary angle units per degree

constants.name: airborneSteerDivisor
constants.unit: divisor applied to the stored turn rate times the frame delta

capabilities: stick heading nudge in the air

cards.name: Gravity, damping and landing
cards.summary: A generic step damps vertical velocity by 0.97 and subtracts a gravity of 0.15 unless a flag skips it; the fall mode uses its own 0.1 gravity, turns slowly and counts fall frames
cards.behavior: A generic velocity step, skipped when a state flag is set, multiplies the vertical velocity by 0.97 raised to the frame delta and then subtracts the stored gravity times the frame delta. The stored gravity is rewritten as 0.15 on every animate call. The fall mode does not use that value: it subtracts a separate global of 0.1 times the frame delta. The fall mode also sets its facing smoothing rate to 40 and its turn rate limit to 0.9, so the character turns slowly in the air. A fall frame counter rises by one each update and saturates at 10. A landing sound and rumble play when the counter is above 5 and a ground-contact flag is set, so a one-frame ground clip does not read as a landing.

constants.name: genericGravity
constants.unit: speed units per update, times the frame delta (1.0 is one 1/60 s step)

constants.name: airDampingPerUpdate
constants.unit: velocity multiplier per update, raised to the frame delta

constants.name: fallFrameSaturation
constants.unit: frame counter, saturates at this value

constants.name: landingSoundWindow
constants.unit: fall frames that must be exceeded for the landing sound

constants.name: fallTurnRateLimit
constants.unit: turn rate limit field (units unverified)

cards.name: Velocity box and step cap
cards.summary: Before the body moves, velocity is clamped to 5 per horizontal axis and 4 vertically, and an upward step is capped at 10 world units
cards.behavior: Just before the body is moved, the two horizontal velocity components are clamped to plus or minus 5 and the vertical one to plus or minus 4 speed units. Each is then multiplied by the frame delta. The vertical step is also capped at 10 world units, but only in the upward direction. Because the clamp is 4, this cap can only act when the frame delta exceeds 2.5. Horizontal steps get no second cap. The clamp is the last thing applied, so earlier systems can overshoot and still end up inside the same limits.

constants.name: horizontalSpeedClamp
constants.unit: speed units per axis per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: verticalSpeedClamp
constants.unit: speed units per update; values are scaled by the frame delta, where 1.0 is one 1/60 s step

constants.name: verticalStepCap
constants.unit: world units, upward step per update only

cards.name: Buoyancy and water current
cards.summary: Water height plus a sine bob sets a buoyancy pull scaled by depth, a 0.1 sink and 0.96 damping settle the body, and vertical velocity is clamped between -4 and 1.4
cards.behavior: The target height is the water surface plus a small sine bob. The difference to the body height is capped above at 25 units, divided by 25 and scaled by 0.13, and added to the vertical velocity times the frame delta. A body above the surface gets a negative value with no lower cap. A constant 0.1 sink is then subtracted, the velocity is multiplied by 0.96 raised to the frame delta, and the result is clamped between -4 and 1.4. Diving can therefore be faster than rising. Surface current is rotated into the character frame and each current component moves toward its target by 0.1 of the remaining gap per update. A ripple effect is spawned from movement events when the water is shallower than 25 units.

constants.name: buoyancyDepthReference
constants.unit: world units, depth cap and divisor

constants.name: buoyancyGain
constants.unit: speed units per update at full depth, times the frame delta

constants.name: waterSinkPerUpdate
constants.unit: speed units per update, times the frame delta

constants.name: waterDampingPerUpdate
constants.unit: velocity multiplier per update, raised to the frame delta

constants.name: waterRiseClamp
constants.unit: speed units per update at 60 Hz (delta-time scaled, 1.0 = one 1/60 s step)

constants.name: waterSinkClamp
constants.unit: speed units per update at 60 Hz (delta-time scaled, 1.0 = one 1/60 s step) (negative is downward)

constants.name: waterCurrentSmoothing
constants.unit: fraction of the remaining gap per update, times the frame delta

cards.name: Ground surface response
cards.summary: Ground surface type changes skid smoothing, applies periodic damage, sinking and conveyor push
cards.behavior: When the ground contact has its surface flag set, the surface type from the palette slot picks the response. Ice sets the target animation speed to 0.055, the facing smoothing scale to 1.75 and the velocity smoothing base to 0.13. Snow sets the target animation speed to 1.0 and the velocity smoothing base to 0.05. Lava and one other numbered type record a damage hit when a timer, reset to 60 and drained by the frame delta, reaches zero. Another numbered type (28) records a hit every 120 frame delta units unless a game bit marks the player immune, and an instant-death type records a lethal hit. A sinking type lowers a sink offset by 0.04 times the frame delta when the character is slow and raises it by 0.05 when moving fast; once the measured depth passes 25 units it takes one health point per update. A conveyor type looks for the nearest conveyor within 500 units and feeds its scroll vector into a push velocity that moves 0.02 of the gap per update. With no conveyor the push decays by 0.9 per update, and values under 0.01 are snapped to zero.

constants.unit: target animation speed, fraction of normal

constants.name: iceFacingSmoothScale

cards.name: Staff boost lift
cards.summary: A staff-triggered vertical ride adds 0.05, then 0.1 per update to upward velocity up to a cap of 5, rises to a probe-derived height, then drags down at 0.98; charging spends 10 magic per chunk
cards.behavior: The boost is a scripted vertical ride started at an interaction target. Setup records the start height and fires a line probe of 100 units from 10 units above the feet along the facing. The target height is a height value from the hit minus 30, or the start height plus 100 when nothing is hit. The first segment adds 0.05 times the frame delta per update to the vertical velocity. The second adds 0.1 and caps the velocity at 5 until the body is above the target height. The third subtracts 0.1 and multiplies the remainder by 0.98 raised to the frame delta, and the state ends when its animation finishes, with vertical velocity reset to zero. While the charge button is held and the charge is not full, the charge level grows by 0.3333 plus 0.5 per frame delta; at 10 it resets and takes 10 magic, clamped to the maximum.

constants.unit: speed units per update, times the frame delta

constants.name: boostSustainedRise
constants.unit: speed units per update, times the frame delta

constants.name: boostRiseCap
constants.unit: speed units, vertical velocity cap

constants.name: boostDescentDrag
constants.unit: velocity multiplier per update, raised to the frame delta

constants.name: boostChargePerUpdate

constants.name: boostSpendThreshold

constants.name: boostMagicCost

cards.name: Staff combo chaining
cards.summary: The staff attack tracks a locked target with a full or a one-twelfth heading correction depending on the swing slot, with rumble on hit and on each swing contact
cards.behavior: A swing is read from a table of move slots, and the move slot index selects how the swing behaves. While a target is locked, the swing heading is corrected toward the target bearing every update: for slot indices 5 to 9 the full bearing is added, and for all other slots a twelfth of it. The attack entry rate is 0.025. A pending hit reaction variant makes the state return an interrupt code with a rumble of 10, and two swing event flags rumble at 5 and play a sound. Combo chain windows and follow-up selection are not covered by the cited lines.

constants.unit: move slot index, inclusive

constants.name: fastSlotLastIndex
constants.unit: move slot index, inclusive

cards.name: Guard stance
cards.summary: Holding the shield trigger plants the character in a hold pose that cannot rotate under the shield
cards.behavior: Guard reads a trigger bit (0x20) and engages only when a combat check passes: the player must not be attacking, climbing, carrying, swimming or locked onto a target, among other flags. Entering the stance switches the staff to shield mode, starts a dedicated hold move with event spacing 8, sets the move rate to 0.01, and zeroes the animation speeds and horizontal velocity. A related branch sets the facing smoothing rate to 20 and the turn rate limits to zero, so the character cannot be turned by the stick while guarding.

constants.name: guardTriggerBit
constants.unit: trigger mask bit

constants.name: guardHoldMoveId
constants.unit: move id

constants.name: guardEventSpacing
constants.unit: frames of event step spacing

constants.name: guardEntryMoveRate

constants.name: guardFacingFollowRate

cards.name: Hit response and knockback clock
cards.summary: The highest priority contact picks a reaction; a hit during recovery does no damage; a new hit sets a 300 knockback timer that drains at the current speed clamped between 1 and 3
cards.behavior: Only the highest priority contact of the update is read. A health value at or below zero is first raised to 1. The priority picks a reaction move, and a counter reaction is chosen when the character is in a normal control state with a locked target. A new knockback sets the knockback timer to 300 and a follow-up hit timer to 200, with an initial drain rate of 1, but only when a recovery flag (bit 0x800) is clear. While that flag is set, a further hit deals no damage and only plays effects. Each update the timer drains by the frame delta times a rate equal to the current speed magnitude clamped between 1 and 3, so a moving character recovers faster. Damage is subtracted from health, clamped between zero and the maximum.

constants.unit: knockback timer start value, drained by the frame delta times a rate

constants.name: knockbackHitClock
constants.unit: follow-up hit timer start value, drained by the frame delta

cards.name: Spell magic gates
cards.summary: Each staff spell has a magic floor and flag-based refusal checks; the quake floor doubles with an upgrade and the maximum magic is clamped at 100
cards.behavior: Spell availability is a pure check that can be called before the player presses anything. The fire blaster needs at least 2 magic and the other blast needs at least 1, both refused while certain move animations, a held object or movement flags are active. The portal spell needs at least 20 magic, a game bit for the ability, and no locked target. The ground quake needs its ability bit and 10 magic, or 20 once the stronger quake bit is set, so the same input becomes a stronger spell. Changes to the maximum magic clamp it between 0 and 100.

cards.name: Scarab wallet capacity
cards.summary: Money is capped by which bag upgrade has been bought, and every grant clamps into that cap
cards.behavior: Each grant adds the amount to the money total and clamps the total between zero and a ceiling chosen by the best bag bit set in the save: 10 before any bag, 50 with the first bag, 100 with the second and 200 with the third. The clamped value is stored and mirrored to a counter game bit. A grant larger than a stored byte value also records that amount in a separate field. A save with more than its ceiling is cut down on the next grant.

cards.name: Wall climb
cards.summary: Wall climbing probes 30 units into the wall along the saved normal and uses a stick-driven speed of 0.034 plus about 0.004 per unit of stick magnitude
cards.behavior: Wall climbing is a separate state with its own move table. While the move progress is at its end value, the state fires a probe of 30 units from the saved position along the wall normal, and uses the hit to refresh the wall data. The climb speed is a base of 0.034 plus 0.003999997 times the stick magnitude, signed by the climb direction, which gives about 0.038 at full stick. A stick magnitude at or below 0.1 stops the climb from advancing in that branch. The state overrides the camera position and refreshes the collision state each update. Other wall data refresh steps are not covered by the cited lines.

constants.name: wallProbeDistance
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: climbBaseSpeed
constants.unit: move rate units per update (unverified)

constants.name: climbSpeedPerStickUnit
constants.unit: move rate per unit of stick magnitude

constants.name: climbIdleMagnitude

cards.name: Ladder slide
cards.summary: A ladder slide keeps its entry speed until it is within ten times that speed of the base, then slows on a square-root profile and snaps to the base when the speed is near zero
cards.behavior: A ladder slide saves the start height, sets the move rate to 0.025 and plays a short transitional move before the descent. In the descent move, the remaining height above the base plus 32 units is compared with ten times the slide speed. While the remaining height is larger, the entry speed is kept. Inside that band the vertical velocity is the negative square root of the slide speed squared over that band, times the remaining height, so it slows toward zero at the base, and when it reaches minus 0.01 or higher the character snaps to the base height and the descent ends. Entering water deeper than 25 units cancels the slide and starts swimming.

constants.name: slideProfileFactor
constants.unit: multiplier on the slide speed that sets the braking band

constants.name: slideBaseOffset
constants.unit: world units above the climb base where braking is measured from

constants.name: slideTerminalVelocity

constants.name: slideMoveRate
constants.unit: move rate field (units unverified)

constants.name: deepWaterDepth

cards.name: Default projection
cards.summary: The default camera uses a 60 degree vertical field of view, a 4:3 aspect ratio, a near plane at 2.5 and a far plane at 10000 that eases over 60 frames when changed
cards.behavior: A new camera state starts with a 60 degree vertical field of view. The aspect ratio is 4:3, the near plane is at 2.5 world units and the far plane at 10000. A far plane change with a non-zero frame count stores the frame count, the start and the target values, and a reset restores 10000 over 60 frames, which is one second at 60 Hz. A zero frame count sets it immediately. The field of view is a camera field, so other code may change it; this card does not claim it is fixed.

constants.unit: ratio, width divided by height

cards.name: Reticle target acquisition
cards.summary: Targets are scanned inside a vertical band and their own range, then ranked by priority and squared distance
cards.behavior: The scan walks the object list and keeps up to 8 candidates, stopping when the eighth is added. It skips the scan in the viewfinder camera mode and when combat targeting is not allowed. A candidate must pass its own eligibility check and have a hit volume priority that is not below the best priority seen so far. The vertical gap, focus height minus hit volume centre height, must lie strictly between -100 and 20 world units, which accepts a target up to 100 above and refuses one more than 20 below; a per-object flag can skip this test. The horizontal squared distance must be under the square of a range read from the hit volume bounds shifted left by 2 bits. Candidates are ordered by priority, highest first, then by squared distance, nearest first. If the best one has the line-of-sight flag, a voxel trace from 20 units above the focus to its joint is made, and a blocked trace discards the lock entirely rather than moving to the next one.

constants.name: minVerticalGap
constants.unit: world units, focus height minus hit volume centre, lower bound exclusive

constants.name: maxVerticalGap
constants.unit: world units, same difference, upper bound exclusive

constants.name: lineOfSightTraceHeight
constants.unit: world units above the focus point

constants.name: targetCandidateCount
constants.unit: candidates, the scan stops when this many are collected

constants.name: rangeBoundsShift
constants.unit: bits, left shift of the bounds value to give the range in world units

cards.name: Camera shake
cards.summary: Shake is a decaying oscillation converted from updates into seconds, with a hard bounce mode for blunt impacts
cards.behavior: The camera has one vertical shake offset. In bounce mode the offset is replaced each update by -0.9 times its previous value for each cooldown step, so it alternates sign and shrinks. In damped mode the offset is the amplitude times an exponential of minus the damping times elapsed time, times a cosine of the elapsed time at the requested frequency. The shake ends when the offset is inside plus or minus 0.1 world units. Elapsed shake time grows by the frame delta divided by 60, so the frequency is in cycles per second.

constants.name: bounceRetain
constants.unit: velocity multiplier per update at 60 Hz

constants.name: shakeFinishThreshold
constants.unit: world units

constants.name: updatesPerSecond
constants.unit: frame delta units per second used to convert shake time

cards.name: Camera mode blend
cards.summary: Mode changes blend across a frame count with a selectable curve, and the per-update correction is capped
cards.behavior: A camera mode request carries a blend length in frames. Blend progress starts at 1, falls each update by the reciprocal of the frame count times the frame delta, and is clamped between 0 and 1. The applied weight is one minus the progress raised to the power 3, 2 or 1 depending on the curve mode (2, 1 or other). Independent of that, a mode can ask for positional smoothing: the step toward the wanted position is a fraction of the remaining distance (0.22 per update through an exponential approach), capped at 3 times the frame delta world units per update. The aim overlay sets curve mode 2 and requests a 30-frame blend, and leaving it requests the default mode over 30 frames.

constants.name: blendSmoothing
constants.unit: fraction of remaining error per update at 60 Hz

constants.name: blendMovementCap
constants.unit: world units per update at 60 Hz, scaled by the frame delta

constants.name: lookOverlayBlendFrames
constants.unit: updates at 60 Hz

constants.name: defaultModeRestoreFrames
constants.unit: updates at 60 Hz

cards.name: Frame clock and loop order
cards.summary: The frame delta is elapsed time times 60, clamped to 6, and forced to zero while the disc error pause is active
cards.behavior: Each frame stops the stopwatch, converts elapsed ticks to milliseconds and multiplies by 60 divided by 1000, so a delta of 1 is one sixtieth of a second. Per-update constants in the player code are written against that unit. The delta is clamped to 6, which caps a stalled frame at a tenth of a second, and it is set to zero while the disc error pause is active. The initial delta value is 1.0. The loop then runs pad sampling, voxel timers and the game update in that order.

constants.name: timestepNormalisation
constants.unit: updates per second used to normalise the frame delta

constants.name: maximumFrameDelta
constants.unit: updates at 60 Hz

constants.name: initialFrameDelta
constants.unit: updates at 60 Hz
